Me thynketh it a cordaunt to resoun
Of eche of hem as it semyth me
And ek in what aray þ
That from the tyme that he ferst began
To rydyn out he louede Chyualrye
Ful worthi was he in hese lordis werre
And therto hadde he / redyn noman ferre
And euere honoured for hese worthynesse
¶ At Alisandir he was whan it was wonne
And ofte tyme / he hadde þe bord begunne
cristene man so ofte / of his degre
In gernage at þe sege ek hadde he be
At manye anobil aryue hadde he be
At mortal bataylis hadde he be fiftene
And for oure feith at tramessene
This ilke worthi knyth hadde ben also
tyme with þe lord of Palatye
And thow that he were worthy he was wys
And of hese port as meke as is a mayde
In al his lyȝf vn to no maner wight
But for to telle ȝow of his aray
Hese hors were goode / but he was not gay
Of fustien he werede a iopo
For he was late come fro
And wente for to don here pilgry
þere was / hese sone aȝong squyer
With lokkis crulle as þey were leyd in presse
Of twenty ȝer / of age he was I gesse
Of hese stature / he was of euene lenthe
wel as of so litil spase
In hope to stondyn / in hese ladygrace
Enbroudit was he / as it were a mede
Al ful of frossche flourys white
He was as frosch as is the monyth of may
Wel coude he sitte on hors /
He slepte no more than doth a nyghtyngale
And karf be forn hese fadir at the table
At that tyme / for he leste ryde soo
And he was clad in cote
A schef of pekok / arwys bryȝte
Vndir his belte he bar ful thryftyly
Wel coude he dresse hese takil ȝemanly
Hese arwis droupede nought with federys lowe
And in his hand he bare a myghty bowe
A not hed hadde he / with a broun vesage
Of wode craft wel coude he al þe usage
Vp on his arm he bar a gay braser
And by his side / a swerd
A notation on the right of the line with two dots and a strike
A Cristofere / on his brest of siluyr schene
An horn he bar þe baudryk was of grene
A foster was he sothli as I gesse
Ther was also a nūne a prieresse
¶ That of here smylyng was ful simple
Here gretteste oth was but be seynt loy
And sche was clepid Madame Eglentyne
Ful wel sche song / þe seruyse of deuyne
Entuned in here nose so semely
And french sche spak ful fayre
For french of parys was to here onknowe
¶ At mete wel I tauȝt / was sche w
Ne wette here fyngyr / in here sause depe
Wel couthe sche carye a morsel /
That no drope ne fel vp on here brest
In curteysie was set ful meche here lyst
Hire ouere lippe wipede sche so klene
Of gres / whan sche dronkyn / hadde her draught
Ful semely aftyr here mete sche raught
And sekyrly sche was of gret disport
And peynede here to contyrfete chere
And to ben holde dygne of reuerence
But for to spekyn of here concience
Sche wolde wepe ȝif that sche seye a mous
Kauȝt in a trappe ȝif it were ded or bledde
With rostid flesch or mylk or wastelbred
But sore wepte sche ȝif on of he
Or ȝif men smot it with a ȝerde smerte
Here nose tretis here eyen greye as glas
But sekyrly / sche hadde a fayr forhed
It was almost a spanne brod I trowe
For hardily sche was not vndir growe
Ful fetys was here cloke as I was war
Of smale corl aboute here arm sche bar
A peyre of bedis I gaudeit al w
on heng a broche of gold so kene
¶ A nothir nonne with here hadde sche
e was a fayr for the maystrye
A manly man to ben an abbot able
Ful manye a deynte hors hadde he in stable
And whan herod men myȝte his brydil here
Gyngelyn in a whistelyng wynd als clere
And ek as loude as doth the chapel belle
There as this lord was kepere of the selle
Be cause that it was old
This ilke monk let olde thy
And held aftyr the newe world the space
He ȝaf not of thattixt a pulled henne
Ne that a monk whan he is rekeles
Is lykened to a fysch that is watyrles
This is to seyne a monk out of hese cloystre
But tilke tixt held he not worth an oystere
Vp on a bok in cloystere alwey to poure
As Austyn bit how schal þᵉ world be servid
Let Austyn han his swynk to hym reservid
Grehondis he hadde as swift as foul i
Was al hese lust for no cost wolde he spare
I sey hese sleuys / purfilid at the hand
And for to festene his hod vndir his schyn
He hadde of gold I wrouȝt a ful coryous pyn
A loue knot in the grettere ende þ
His hed was ballyd that schon as ony glas
And ek hese face as he hadde ben enoynt
He was a lord ful fat
That stemyd as a furneys of a led
Hese botis souple / his hors in gret estat
Now serteynly he was a fayr prelat
He nas not pale as a forpynnede gost
A fat swan louede he best of ony rost
In alle the orderys foure is non that can
He hadde mad ful manye a maryage
Of ȝonge wemen at hese owene cost
On to his ordere he was a noble post
For he hadde power of confessioun
For of hese ordere he was licencyat
He was an esi man to ȝeue pena
There as he wiste to han a good petauns
Vnto pore orderis for to ȝeue
For ȝif he ȝaf he durste make auaunt
He wiste that a man was repentaunt
For manye a man so hard is of hese herte
He may not wepe though hy
¶ Hise tipet was ay farsed ful of knyuys
And pynnys for to ȝeuyn fayre wywes
And serteynli he hadde a merye throte
Of ȝeddyngis he bar vttyrli the prys
His nekke whit was as the flour delis
Therto he strong was as a chaumpio
He knew the tauernys wel in euery toun
Bet than a laser or a bakystere
For vn to swich a worthi man as he
Acordith not as by his faculte
To haue with swiche sike men a queynta
It is not honest it may not auauce
For to dele with non swich parayle
Ther was no man now so v
For thow a wedewe hadde not a scho
Ȝit wolde he haue a ferthyng er he wente
His purchas was wel betyr than hese rente
And rage he couthe as it were ryȝt a whelp
In louedayis there couthe he mekil help
For there he was not lik a cloysterer
With a thredbare kope as is a
But he was lik a m
Of double worstede was hese semeli kope
ded as a belle / out of the presse
what he lipsede for hese wantoūnesse
To make hese engelisch swete vp on his tunge
ge whan that he hadde su
As don the sterrys / in the frosty nyght
t was there with a forkede berd
In motle an heigh on horse he sat
Vp on his hed a fla
Hese resoun he spak ful plesauntly
Sounynge alwey the cres of hese wy
He wolde the se / were kept for ony thyng
This worthi man ful wel his wit be sette
There wiste no man that he was in dette
So estatli was he of hese gou
Forsothe he was a worthy man withal
But sothe to seyn I not how men hy
A clerk there was of oxsenforthe also
That vnto logyk hadde longe I go
As lene was hese hors as is a rake
Ne was so wordely for to hauyn offys
For hym was lefere to haue at hese bedis hed
I clad in blak or red
Þan robis ryche or fedele or gay sautrie
hadde but lityl gold in cofre
he myȝte of hese frendis hente
And besily gan for þe soulys preye
Of stodie tok he most kep
Not a word spak he more þa
Sounynge in moral uertu was hese speche
A seriaunt of the lawe bothe war
That oftyn hadde ben at þᵉ paruys
He was also ryche of excellence
He semede swich hese wordis were so wyse
Iustyse he was ful oftyn in asyse
So gret a purchasour was neu
His purchase myȝte not ben enfect
e so besy aman as he þere nas
he semede besiere þan he was
the tyme of kyng welyam were falle
Ther coude no man pynche at hese writyng
y statut coude he pleyn be rote
He rod but homely in a medely cote
Gyrt with a seynt of silk w
Of hese aray telle I no lengere tale
¶ A fran̄keleyn was in hese cu
Whit was hese berd as is þe daysie
Wel louede be þᵉ morwe a soppe in wyn
To leuyn in delit was euere hese wone
Seynt Ielion he was in that cuntre
Hese bred hese ale was alwey aftyr on
A betere enuynede man was nower non
It snowede in his mouth of
Of alle deynteis that men coude þynk
Aftyr þᵉ sundery sesenys of the ȝer
Ful manye a fat perterych hadde he i
Wo was hese cook / but ȝif hese sauce were
Ful ofte tyme he was knght of the schyre
Heng at hese gyrdil whit as morwy
And þey were clothid alle in on lyuere
Here knyues were chapid not with bras
To sittyn In a ȝilde halle on a deys
ych for the wisdam that he can
Was schaply for to ben an aldirman
For catel hade þey I now
And ek here wyuys wolde it wel assente
And ellis serteyn weryn þey to blame
It is ful fayr to be clepid madame
And gon to vigilis al be fore
And han a mental ryalliche I bore
Wel coude he knowe a drauȝt of londen ale
But gret harm was it as it semede me
That on hese schene a mormal hadde he
For ouȝt I wot he was of dertemouthe
He rod up on a rou
ne of faldynge to the kne
ge on a lace hadde he
Aboute his nekke vndir his arm ado
The hote somyr hadde mad his hew al broun
And serteynli he was a good felawe
Ful manye a drauȝt of weyn hadde he I drawe
From burdeux ward whil that the chapman slep
Of nyce consience tok he none kep
But of hese craft to rekene wel hese tydis
pest hadde his berd ben schake
He knew alle þe hauenys as þey were
Fro gotlond to the kape of fenystere
In al þis world was ther non hy
Hepte hese pacient a ful gret del
In houres by his Magik naturel
Of hese ymagis / for hese pacient
He knew the cause of eu
Were it hot or cold or moyst or dreye
Anon he ȝaf the seke man hese bote
Ful redy hadde he sese apotecaryis
Here frenschepe was not newe to begy
Wel knew he the olde exculapijs
Of hese diete mesurable was he
For it was of non superfluyte
His stody was wol lytyl in the bible
in pers he clad was al
And ȝit he was but esy of dispence
He kepte that he wan in pestelence
For gold in phisik is a cardial
Therfore he louede gold in special
A good wif was there of beside bathe
Of cloth makyng sche hade swich an hand
In al the parich wif was there non
That to the offerynge to fore her schulde gon
And ȝif þere dede serteyn so wroth was sche
That sche was out of alle charite
Here couercheis ful fyne were of ground
I durste swere þey weyedyn a pound
That on a sunday weryn vp on here hed
Here hosyn weryn of fyn skarlet red
Sche was a worthi woman al here lyue
Husbondis at cherche dore sche hadde fyue
But þerof nedith not to speke as nouthe
And thryes hadde sche ben at Ierusalem
Sche hadde passed manye a strong strem
Sche couthe meche of wonderyng be þ
Gat toþed was sche sothly for to seye
As brod as is abokeler or a targe
A fot mental a boute here hepis large
And on here fet a peyre of sporys scharpe
In felauschepe wel coude sche lawe
Of remedijs of loue / sche knew per schau
For sche coude of that art the olde dau
A good man was there of religiou
But riche he was of holy thouȝt
He was also a lerned man a clerk
That cristis gospel trewely wolde teche
Hese parischiens deuoutly wolde he teche
He couthe in lityl thyng han suffisiau
But he ne lyfte not for reyn ne thondir
In seknesse nor in myschif to visite
The fertheste in hese parich meche
ple to hese schep he ȝaf
Out of the gospel he to wordis cauȝte
And this figure he addede þ
That ȝif gold rustede what schal yryn do
That ȝif a pryst be foul on who
And schame it is ȝif a pryst take kep
Wel outhe a prest ensaumple for to ȝeue
By hese clennesse how hese schep schulde leue
He sette not hese benefys to hyre
An let hese schep acumbrit in the myre
And ran to lundene vn to seynt poulys
To seke hym a chauntriye for soulys
Or with a broþerhed to be with holde
So that þe wolf ne made it not myscarie
He was not to synful men dispitous
Ne of hese speche daungerous ne digne
To drawyn folk to heuyn be clennesse
Be good ensaumple this was hese besynesse
But ȝif it were ony persone obstynat
What so he were of hey or low estat
Hym wolde he snybbyn scharpli for the nonys
A bettyr pryst I trowe neuere non is
He waytid aftyr no pompe ne reuerence
Ne makid him a spisede concience
He taughte but fyrst he folwede it hym selue
With hym þere was a plowman that was hese broþer
That hadde led of donge manye a fodir
God louede he best with al hese hole herte
At alle tymys thow hym gamenede or smerte
And thanne his nyȝhe-bour riȝt as hym selue
For cristis sake for / euery pore wyght
With-outyn hyre / ȝif it leye in his myȝt
Hese tythis payede he ful fayre
In a tabbard he rod vp on a mere
¶ a Reve. a. Mellere. a Sunour. a Pardonnere.
myn self there were no mo
The meller was a strong carl for the nonys
ful big he was of braun
That preuyd he wel for ouyr al þere he cam
At wrastelynge he wolde haue alwey the ram
Ther nas no dore that he wolde heue of harre
Oor breke it at a rennyng with hese hed
His berd as ony sowe or fox was red
And þerto brod as þow it were a spade
Vp on the cop ryȝt of hese nose he hade
theron stod a tuft of herys
Red as the brostelis of a sowys erys
a bokeler bar he bi hese syde
And that was most of synne ⁊ harlotrye
And that he hadde a tabbard of good
A bagge pipe wel couthe he blowe
And þerwithal he brouȝte / vs out of tounne
A gentyl maunciple was þere of a temple
Of whiche acatouris myȝte take exsaumple
For to ben wys in beyinge of uytayle
For where that he payede or tok be tayle
Algate he waytide so in hese acate
That he was ay be forin
Now is not that of god / a ful fayr grace
That swich a lewede manys wit schal pace
The wisdam of an hep / of lernede men
Of maystrys hadde he mo þan thryis ten
Of whiche þere were a doseyn i
Worthi to ben styward of rente
Of ony lord that is in yngelond
Or leue as skarsely as hy
In ony cas that myȝte falle or happe
The reue was a sclendere colerik man
Hese berd was schaue as nygh as eu
His her was by hese erys ful roude I schorn
His top was dokkyd as a pryst be forn
Y lik a staf ther was no calf I sene
Wel couthe he kepe a gerner
There non auditour couthe on hy
Wel wiste he be þe droute
His lordis schep hese net hese deyerye
Hese swyn hese hors hese stoor
Was holly in þis revis gouerny
þat his lord was twenty ȝer of age
Ther nas bayle herde ne oþ
The were adred of hym as of the deþ
Hese wonyng was ful fayre / vp on an heth
With grene treis I schadewid was hese place
He couthe betere þan hese lord purchase
Ful riche he was a storid preuyly
Hese lord. wel couthe he plese subtily
In ȝouthe he hadde lernyd a good mystir
He was a wol good wryȝte a carpenter
This reue sat vp on a ful good stot
A long surcote of pers vp on he hadde
And bi hese syde he bar a rusty blade
Of norfolke was þis reue of whiche I telle
Be syde a toun men clepe baldiswelle
Tukkede he was as is a frere aboute
And euere he rod þᵉ hemereste of oure route
A somnour was þere with vs in that plase
That hadde a fer red cherubynys face
For sausefleme he was with eyen narwe
Of hese vesage chylderyn weryn a ferid
Ther nas quyk siluyr litarge ne bronston
Boras seruse ne oyle of tartre non
That hym myȝte helpyn of hese whelkys white
Ne of the knobbis sittynge on hese schekes
And for to drynkyn strong wyn red as blod
And whan he wel dronkyn hadde þe wyn
Thanne wolde he speke no word but latyn
A fewe termys hadde he to or thre
That he hadde lernyd out of sum decre
No wondir he herde it al the day
And ek ȝe knowe wel that a Iay
Kan clepe watte as wel as can the pope
But who so couthe in oþere þyngis hym grope
Thanne hadde he spent al hese philosophie
Ay questio quod Iurys wolde he crye
A betere felawe schulde men not fynnde
He wolde suffere for a quart of wyn
A good felawe to haue hese concubyn
Ful pryuyly a fync ek couthe he pulle
And ȝif he fond ower a good felawe
He wolde techyn hym to haue non awe
In swich cas of the erchedekenys curs
But ȝif a manys soule were in hese pors
For in hese purs he schulde ponyschid be
Purs is the erchedekynys helle seyde he
But wel I wot he lyeþ ryȝt in dede
Of cursyng owyth eche gilty man drede
For curs wele sle ryȝt as asoylyng sauyth
And also war hym of a sygnyficauyth
In daunger hadde he at hese owene gyse
The ȝonge gerlys of the diosyse
A garlond hade he set vp on hese hed
As gret as it were for an ale stake
A bokeler hadde he mad hym of a cake
With hym there rod a Ioly pardounner
That streyt was comyn from the court of rome
Ful loude he song loue come hedir come
This somnour bar to hym a stif bordoun
Was neuere triompe half of so gret a soun
This pardounner hade her as ȝelw as ony wax
But smothe it heng as doþ a strik of flex
Be ouncis heng hese lokkys þat he hadde
And þerwith he hese schulderys ouerspradde
But thenne it lay be culpounnys on
And hod for Iolite werede he non
For it was trussed vp in hese walet
Hym thouȝte he rod al of the newe iet
Discheuele saf his cappe he rod al bare
Sweche glarynge. eyen. hadde. he as an hare
A vernykele hadde he sowyd vp on hese cappe
A uoys he hath as smal as haþ a got
No berd hadde he ne neu
As smothe it was / as it were late schaue
I trowe he were a geldyns or a mare
For in his male he hadde a pilwe bere
he seyde was oure lady ueyl
He seyde he hadde a gobet of þe seyl
That seynt petyr hadde whan þ
He hadde a cros / of latoun . ful of stonys
And in a glas he hadde piggis bonys
Vp on a day he gat hy
But trewely to tellyn at the laste
He was in cherche a noble ecclesiaste
But aldirbest he song an offratory
For wel he wiste whan that song was sunge
Now haue I told ȝow sothly in a clause
In southwerk at this ientil ostelry
That hyȝte the tabbard faste by þ
But now is tyme to ȝow for to telle
How that we beryn vs that ilke nyȝt
Whan that we were in that ostelrye alyȝt
And aftyr wole I telle of oure viage
But fyrst I prey ȝow of ȝoᵘre curteysye
That ȝe narette not myn velanye
Ne thow I speke here wordis properly
Who so schal telle a tale aftyr a man
He mote reherse as nyh as eu
yche a word ȝif it be in his charge
Or elle he mote telle his tale ontrewe
He may not spare al they he wer
He mote as wel seyn on word as a noþ
self ful brode in holy wryt
And wel ȝe wote no velany is it
Ek plato seyth ho so can hy
The wordyˢ mote be chose to the dede
Also I preye ȝow to forȝeue it me
Al haue I not set folk in here degre
Here in this tale al as þey schulde stonde
Myn wit is schort ȝe may wel vndyrstonde
Gret chere mad oure ost vs eu
And to the soper sette he vs a non
A semely man oure ost was w
For to ben a marchal of an hal
A large man he was with eyne stepe
